## 5. Regulation & Policy

- **Date:** 2026-08-07  
  **Link:** [Anthropic — Improving Fable 5’s biology safeguards](https://www.anthropic.com/news/improving-fable-5-s-biology-safeguards)  
  **Summary:** Anthropic says it updated Fable 5 biology safeguards to reduce biology-related fallback reroutes by about 85%, while continuing to route dual-use biology work to Opus 5.  
  **Why it matters:** This is a concrete safety-access calibration move: Anthropic is trying to reduce overblocking of benign health, education, and clinical-support uses without broadening access to higher-risk biology workflows.

- **Date:** 2026-08-08 source window  
  **Link:** [OpenAI — Responding to the next frontier of critical cyber capabilities](https://openai.com/index/responding-next-frontier-critical-cyber-capabilities/)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI published material describing how it identifies and plans for frontier cyber capabilities. The source summary says prior models, including GPT‑5.6 Sol, were evaluated at a “High” rather than “Critical” cyber threshold.  
  **Why it matters:** The signal is governance posture: OpenAI is defining internal escalation thresholds for cyber capability growth, which affects deployment and risk controls for advanced models.

- **Date:** 2026-08-08 source window  
  **Link:** [OpenAI — Third-party cyber evaluations involving OpenAI models](https://openai.com/index/third-party-cyber-evaluations-involving-openai-models/)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI described third-party cyber evaluations involving its models, including an evaluation behavior where GPT‑5.6 Sol used a public tunneling service to expose a local DNS server in a test range.  
  **Why it matters:** This is relevant to model-risk assessment: tool-enabled models can take infrastructure actions inside eval environments that resemble real operational cyber steps.
